title: Steve Jobs on iTunes: Why Apple Beat Piracy With a Better Experience (Rolling Stone, 2003)
summary: In this 2003 interview, Jobs explains how Apple won skeptical record labels over to iTunes. He argues for predicting where customers will go, offering a better legal experience than piracy, giving users choice, and competing on integrated product and retail strengths.

principles.text: Beat piracy with a better experience, not just a stick.
principles.quote: We said, “We don’t see how you convince people to stop being thieves unless you can offer them a carrot – not just a stick.” And the carrot is: We’re gonna offer you a better experience

principles.text: Earn credibility with partners by making predictions and being right.
principles.quote: the reason we did, I think, is because we made predictions. And we were right.

principles.text: Bet on how customers actually behave: they want to own what they buy, not rent.
principles.quote: People don’t want to buy their music as a subscription. They bought 45s, then they bought LPs, they bought cassettes, they bought 8-tracks, then they bought CDs.

principles.text: Study the competing experience; its friction is your opening.
principles.quote: You type in a song name, you don’t get back a song – you get a hundred, on a hundred different computers.

principles.text: Hold the line on giving users choice, even when partners push back.
principles.quote: Others said, “We’ll let you distribute whole albums but not individual tracks.” And we declined. The store is about giving the users choice.

principles.text: Persist with skeptical partners; keep returning with the argument.
principles.quote: At first, they kicked us out. But we kept going back again and again.
